newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania says to sell airline, telecoms firm.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania says to sell airline, telecoms firm.

text.p: The Lithuanian government on Wednesday said it planned to privatise its national airline and telecommunications company by international tender during 1997-1998.
The government press office said in a statement that the government had approved a 1997-1998 privatisation list containing 14 companies including Lithuanian Airlines and Lithuanian Telecom.

The other companies on the list included state-owned oil company Lithuanian Oil, which is still being formed, smaller state airline Aviation Company Lithuania, the Lithuanian Radio and Television Centre, Klaipeda Sea Cargo Company from Lithuania's main port of Klaipeda and Lithuanian Sea Shipping.
Lithuania has been seen as a laggard in the Baltic states as its privatisation programme has fallen behind that of Latvia and Estonia.
But the new right-wing government of Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius has pledged to speed privatisation and attract more foreign capital.

The list also included Geonafta, an oil exploration company, a ship cargo company, the West Ship Repair Company, both based in Klaipeda, and other smaller companies, including a multi-story hotel in the capital Vilnius.
The statement did not give an estimated value for the companies in the privatisation.
